summary: When IPv6 datagrams using LoWPAN encapsulation (RFC 4944) travel over Layer 2 technologies such as Ethernet, the receiver must be able to recognize them. This informational document records the Ethertype that was assigned for that purpose.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7973 records the IEEE Ethertype assigned to LoWPAN encapsulation. A receiver can use this identifier to recognize IPv6 datagrams carried in that format.

questions: what ethertype is assigned for lowpan
how to identify lowpan encapsulated ipv6 on ethernet
subtitle: An IEEE Ethertype identifies IPv6 datagrams using LoWPAN encapsulation.

tldr.problem: A receiver using a Layer 2 technology with protocol dispatch needs to identify an IPv6 datagram that uses LoWPAN encapsulation.
tldr.mechanism: The IETF requested an Ethertype assignment from IEEE. IEEE assigned 0xA0ED, decimal 41197, to LoWPAN encapsulation.
tldr.outcome: The assignment provides an identifier for LoWPAN-encapsulated IPv6 datagrams carried over Layer 2 technologies that use Ethertypes.

today: RFC 7973 is an Informational document recording IEEE's assignment of Ethertype 0xA0ED for LoWPAN encapsulation. It does not specify changes to the encapsulation itself.

sections.title: Why LoWPAN Needs an Ethertype
sections.content: LoWPAN encapsulation is a format for IPv6 datagrams defined in RFC 4944. The original intended Layer 2 technology, IEEE 802.15.4, does not provide a protocol switch in its Layer 2 headers. Other Layer 2 technologies and tools need a protocol identifier to recognize the encapsulation.
sections.plainLanguage: Some network links use a field to say what kind of data follows. A unique identifier lets those links recognize LoWPAN-encapsulated IPv6 datagrams.

sections.title: The IEEE Assignment
sections.content: The IETF requested an Ethertype assignment from IEEE, and IEEE assigned 0xA0ED for IPv6 datagrams using LoWPAN encapsulation. RFC 7973 records the decimal value as 41197 and the description as “LoWPAN encapsulation” in the IEEE 802 Numbers registry.
sections.plainLanguage: IEEE assigned the value 0xA0ED to LoWPAN encapsulation. The registry also lists its decimal form, 41197.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: RFC 7973 only reports the Ethertype assignment. It says the assignment has no incremental security implications beyond those of the relevant protocols.
sections.plainLanguage: The document assigns an identifier. It does not add security properties to LoWPAN or IPv6.
